Create a data-entry template

Source: R/template.R
delphi_template.Rd

Writes an empty file in the DelphiR format, ready to be filled in with the ratings of a Delphi study and imported with read_delphi(). Excel templates contain four sheets:

  • ratings, with the column headers of the chosen layout;

  • items, listing the item codes, next to which the full statements can be written;

  • comments, for the written comments of the experts, one per row (see delphi_add_comments());

  • instructions, explaining how to fill in the template, with an example and the R code to import it.

CSV templates contain the ratings table only.

Usage

delphi_template(
  file,
  items = 10,
  layout = c("wide", "long"),
  indicators = c("impact", "probability"),
  overwrite = FALSE
)

Arguments

file

Path of the template, ending in .xlsx or .csv.

items

Number of items, or a character vector of item codes. By default, ten items coded E1 to E10.

layout

"wide" (default), with one row per expert, round and indicator and one column per item, or "long", with one row per rating.

indicators

Indicator labels shown in the instructions, for example c("impact", "probability").

overwrite

Whether to replace an existing file.

Value

The path of the template, invisibly.

Details

Excel templates require the writexl package. Every row of the ratings sheet must identify the expert and the round; in the wide layout, each row also names the indicator to which its ratings refer. The same expert should keep the same identifier in every round, so that individual opinions can be followed across rounds.

See also

read_delphi() to import the completed template.

Examples

# \donttest{
if (requireNamespace("writexl", quietly = TRUE)) {
  path <- delphi_template(file.path(tempdir(), "delphi_template.xlsx"),
                          items = 8, indicators = c("impact", "probability"))
  path
}
#> [1] "/tmp/Rtmpeb3Zvn/delphi_template.xlsx"
# }
# A CSV template in the long layout
path <- delphi_template(file.path(tempdir(), "delphi_long.csv"), layout = "long")
readLines(path)
#> [1] "\"expert\",\"round\",\"indicator\",\"item\",\"value\""
